> Do not change `<vN-1>` unless a shared generator forces the change, and say so when it does.

Evidence:

- This rule allows a change to the frozen generation when a shared generator forces it. NR-27 requires the previous generation to be byte-identical to its release branch.

## FR-04: This package is a workspace member driven from the root `[STALE]`

> This package is a member of the workspace, and every verb runs from the root through a `make` target.

Old number: 1.4.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/foundry.toml:3` and `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/remappings.txt:3-4` show that `forge-std` resolves from the local soldeer `dependencies/`, not from `../../node_modules`. Fix: correct the dependency sentence. Only the npm packages resolve from `../../node_modules`.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-28: Must every npm verb have a `make` target? `test:fork-debug` has none.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-36: Does a rule that repeats one sentence of another rule count as `[CONFLICT]`?

Issues: I-28, I-36.

`foundry/forge-fhevm-std` and its `pkg/` are
in the sdk root's `workspaces` and in `npm-manifest.json` (`@fhevm/forge-std-dev` / `@fhevm/forge`), so
`node_modules` is the root's — `libs` and `remappings.txt` point at `../../node_modules`, never at a local
copy — and every verb has a `make` name: `compile-forge-std` (after `compile-cleartext-v-cur`, because the
payload is copied from `<vN>`), `lint-forge-std`, `test-forge-std`, and the opt-in `test-forge-std-fork`,
`-fork-url`, `-anvil`. `make generate` and `make clean-generated` run this package AFTER `<vN>`, so
`check-generated` proves the whole chain in the diagram of [FR-20](../entries/FR-20.md), and `make check-pre` grades the package.json,
scripts, lockfile and lint policy by the workspace rules ([the npm rules](../../../fhevm-npm/rules/README.md)). The published
payload has a consumer test (`test-consumer/esm`, [NR-54](../../../fhevm-npm/rules/entries/NR-54.md) there), and it is A FOUNDRY PROJECT, not a Node
script: `package.json` installs `@fhevm/forge` by name next to `forge-std` (a git dependency, pinned to the
tag this package vendors), `@fhevm/solidity` and `encrypted-types`; `remappings.txt` points every prefix into
`node_modules`; `src/AplusB.sol` is the dApp and `test/AplusB.t.sol` inherits `TestFhevm` to encrypt, run and
decrypt against it. `npm test` there is `forge build && forge test`. Its `foundry.toml` restates the `[fmt]`
policy inline rather than extending `foundry.base.toml` (a standalone project is copied out of the tree —
the one exception of [NR-30](../../../fhevm-npm/rules/entries/NR-30.md)), so `forge lint` and `forge test` work only after `npm install` in the copy.

## FR-05: `shared/` never touches the forge VM `[CONFLICT]`

> Code in `shared/` never uses the forge VM or a cheatcode.

Old number: 2.1.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- Conflicts with FR-29.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-29: Does "carries `Forge` in its name" apply to every file in `pkg/src` that uses the VM, or only to host source and `_host/`?

Issues: I-13, I-29.

No `IForgeVm`, no `FORGE_VM_ADDRESS`, no cheatcodes.
Those files are compiled into the _deployed_ contracts; a cheatcode there is a contract that cannot
exist on chain. Anything needing the VM goes in `pkg/forge/src/` (payload) or `pkg/src/` (this
package), and carries `Forge` in its name — see [FR-29](../entries/FR-29.md) to [FR-31](../entries/FR-31.md). Which of the two may import `forge-std` is rule [FR-20](../entries/FR-20.md).

<a id="fr-06"></a>

## FR-06: Symmetry wherever it costs nothing `[HOLD]`

> Two things that do the same job take the same shape, order, and names.

Old number: 2.2.

Check: impossible.

The three decryption paths, the two user paths, the
`Args` structs, the `OnForkStack` / `OnCleartextStack` pairs: if two things do the same job they take
the same shape, in the same order, with the same names. A reader who learns one has learned the
other. Break symmetry only for a measured reason — a stack-too-deep, a gas cost — and write that
reason where the asymmetry is.

<a id="fr-07"></a>

## FR-07: One owner per piece of global state `[CONFLICT]`

> Each piece of forge cheatcode state has exactly one owner.

Old number: 2.3.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- Conflicts with FR-34.
- `CleartextForgeFHEVMExecutor.sol` (`cast`, `trivialEncrypt` and others) resumes gas metering unconditionally after its own work, so a test's own `vm.pauseGasMetering` section is switched back on. Line not recorded. Fix: depends on D10.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-35: Is an accurate history passage, such as the removed event replay, a retired passage or acceptable rationale?
- Pending owner decision, issue I-36: Does a rule that repeats one sentence of another rule count as `[CONFLICT]`?
- Pending owner decision, issue I-37: Does the gas-metering rule bind the cleartext mock contracts and the `view` helpers?

Issues: I-12, I-13, I-35, I-36, I-37.

Forge's cheatcode state is shared by everything in a
test; two owners is a bug that surfaces far from its cause.

- **Gas metering** — owned by `ForgeVmBase.unmetered`, applied at every public entry of
  `StdFhevmEncrypt` / `StdFhevmDecrypt` / `StdFhevmDecryptPublic`. Nothing below an entry point may
  call `pauseGasMetering` / `resumeGasMetering`: an inner `resume` re-enables metering in the middle
  of the outer scope and nothing reports it (measured: 0 gas before the inner call, 93k after). The
  modifier is depth-counted because entry points call each other, and its counter is in transient
  storage because a cold `SSTORE` is itself charged to the test.
- **The recorded-log buffer** — NOT THIS SDK'S, and the entry is kept only so the constraint is not
  reinvented. The replay had to see every FHE event or lose track of a value, so the buffer had two
  readers: recording was armed in the constructor, `fhevm.getRecordedLogs()` drained it once and served
  both, and a test reaching for `vm.getRecordedLogs()` starved the replay — the next decryption then
  failed on a handle it had never seen. A forked stack holds its own plaintexts now ([FR-19b](../entries/FR-19b.md)), so the SDK
  neither arms recording nor reads the buffer, and `vm.recordLogs()` means what forge says it means.
- **The cleartext store** — owned by the STACK, not by this SDK, which is what replaced the event
  processor. Each execution context has its own because it IS chain state: forge's fork isolation gives
  the guarantee the processor needed a lifecycle rule to get, and a snapshot revert takes the store back
  with everything else. Read through `stack.plaintexts`, which is always the executor now.
- **The current stack** — owned by `fhevm` (`protocol()` / `setProtocol`). The local cleartext stack by
  default, from `StdFhevm`'s constructor; moved by every fork operation on `fhevm` ([FR-16](../entries/FR-16.md)).
- **The gas-metering depth counter** — owned by `fhevm` (`enterUnmetered` / `exitUnmetered`), in ITS
  transient storage. `TSTORE` is per address, so a counter per contract is two counters, and the inner
  scope's exit resumes metering inside the outer one. `StdFhevmBase` routes the modifier's hooks there.
- **Everything fork-related** — drift check, stack resolution, preparation, the upgrade to cleartext,
  pointing — is `fhevm`'s (`ensureForkPrepared`, …). A `StdFhevm*` mixin inherits `StdFhevmBase` alone and
  makes ONE `fhevm` call at each entry; no mixin knows how a fork is prepared. `fhevm` holds a COPY of
  the chain table's addresses, pushed by
  `StdFhevm` at construction and after every `setFhevmChain`, for resolving a URL-only fork; the table
  itself (RPC URLs, overrides) stays the test's.

## FR-08: Addresses are resolved, never hardcoded `[STALE]`

> The SDK resolves every protocol address at run time and never hardcodes one.

Old number: 2.4.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- No SDK code calls `currentConfig()`, checked when the four taggings were merged. File and line not recorded. Fix: name the function that the SDK resolves addresses through.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-36: Does a rule that repeats one sentence of another rule count as `[CONFLICT]`?

Issues: I-12, I-36.

Everything asks `LibFhevmProtocol.currentConfig()`:
ACL, executor, KMS verifier, input verifier (read off the executor) and the plaintext source. A
compile-time constant is correct for exactly one deployment and silently wrong on every fork — and
the ACL address is mixed into every handle, so a wrong one produces handles no chain will recognise.

## FR-10: Group helpers by family `[VIOLATED]`

> Each library owns one concern, and its name says which.

Old number: 2.6.

Check: impossible.

Evidence:

- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/StdFhevmCheats.sol:200-210` shows `_typeName`, which repeats the eight type names of `LibFheType.toString` (`host-contracts-cleartext/v14/pkg/src/cleartext/shared/LibFheType.sol:42-52`) and differs only in the fallback. Fix: call `LibFheType.toString` and keep only the numeric fallback in the SDK.

Issues: I-16.

One concern, one library, and the name says which concern:
`LibFhevmHandle` owns the internal handle format (chain id, index, type byte, version), `LibFheType`
owns the type enum and its widths, `LibKmsVerifier` owns EIP-712 digests and decryption payloads,
`LibInputVerifier` owns input proofs. A helper that fits an existing family goes there, even when it
is one line; a helper that fits none is a sign a family is missing, not a reason to put it anywhere.
The same rule split `LibFheType` out of two duplicate `FheType` declarations and merged
`CleartextHandle` into `LibFhevmHandle` — both had produced silent drift first.

<a id="fr-12"></a>

## FR-12: A user never hears the word handle `[VIOLATED]`

> The public API speaks in encrypted types and clear values, never in `bytes32` handles.

Old number: 2.8.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- Ten user-visible messages in `LibFhevmFail.sol` use the word handle. Lines not recorded. Fix: reword the messages.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-33: Are the 25 `bytes32` batch overloads of `decrypt` and `decryptPublic` the rule's "type cannot be known" exception?

Issues: I-12, I-33.

The public API speaks in encrypted types — `euint32`,
`ebool`, `eaddress` — and in clear values. A `bytes32` handle is how the stack stores a value, not how
a test talks about one: `plaintextOf(euint32)`, `forkUnknown(euint32, uint32)`, `decrypt(euint32, …)`.
An entry point that takes or returns a `bytes32` is a leak, and the fix is a typed overload, not a doc
comment — the only exception is a case where the type genuinely cannot be known at the call site, and
that case says so in its name. `unwrap` in a test is the symptom; a `seedCleartext(bytes32, uint256)`
with no typed overload is what this rule was written after.

<a id="fr-13"></a>

## FR-13: A value is read from the stack that computed it `[CONFLICT]`

> Decryptions and cheats read a value from the executor that computed it.

Old number: 2.9.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- Conflicts with FR-19b.
- The heading of FR-19b states the lead of this rule again: a value is read from the executor. The code agrees with both at `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/FhevmVm.sol:1265`. Fix: keep one statement.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-35: Is an accurate history passage, such as the removed event replay, a retired passage or acceptable rationale?
- Pending owner decision, issue I-36: Does a rule that repeats one sentence of another rule count as `[CONFLICT]`?

Issues: I-13, I-35, I-36.

`decrypt`, `decryptPublic` and the cheats
ask the executor, which holds the cleartext of everything it computed — no replay, no draining, no order
to get wrong. This rule used to say the opposite: every entry drained the recorded logs into an event
processor first, and an entry point that forgot failed on a fork with `CleartextEventUnknownHandle`, far
from the line that forgot. That whole hazard is gone with the processor ([FR-19b](../entries/FR-19b.md)), and with it the
fork-switch drain — a store cannot replay fork A's events onto fork B if it never replays anything.

WHAT REPLACED THE HAZARD is a smaller one, in the other direction: a handle the stack did NOT compute.
On a fork those are ordinary — the chain is full of them — and `forkUnknown` states one, or a per-type
policy answers for all of them. See [FR-19c](../entries/FR-19c.md).

<a id="fr-14"></a>

## FR-14: The SDK is user friendly, always `[VIOLATED]`

> Each public entry is one typed call in the vocabulary of the FHE library, with nothing for the user to wire.

Old number: 2.10.

Check: impossible.

Evidence:

- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/StdFhevmDecryptPublic.sol:138` shows `decryptPublic(bytes32 a, bytes32 b)`, a public entry that takes raw `bytes32` where the rule promises typed arguments. FR-12 counts the same defect. Fix: fix it with FR-12. The fix depends on D6.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-33: Are the 25 `bytes32` batch overloads of `decrypt` and `decryptPublic` the rule's "type cannot be known" exception?

Issues: I-16, I-33.

forge-fhevm-std is what a dApp developer types in a
test, not an internal of the mock stack. Every public entry is judged by the line a user writes: one
call, typed arguments, the vocabulary of the FHE library they already use (`euint32`, `encryptUint32`,
`decrypt`), nothing to wire and nothing to know about how the stack works underneath. The measure is
the fork test that reads as five lines — get, `forkUnknown`, encrypt, call, `decryptPublic` — where the
same work once took an `eventProcessor()`, an `unwrap`, a manual replay and three hardcoded addresses.
When a step is needed for the protocol, the SDK does it (the upgrade to cleartext, the signer swap, the
address resolution); when a step is needed from the user, one call with a plain name does it. A helper that is
correct but awkward is not done — [FR-12](../entries/FR-12.md) and [FR-13](../entries/FR-13.md) are this rule applied twice.

<a id="fr-15"></a>

## FR-15: A setup failure tells the user how to fix it `[VIOLATED]`

> A setup failure reverts with a loud message that says what happened, why, and the line that fixes it.

Old number: 2.11.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/LibFhevmFail.sol:65` shows the FORK DRIFT message, which tells the user that the FHE events were not drained. Nothing drains since the replay was removed (`foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/FhevmVm.sol:599-603`). Fix: correct the FORK DRIFT text.
- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/internal/StdFhevmChains.sol.template:153,157,164,181,187,255,260` (generated into `pkg/src/StdFhevmChains.sol`) show that a wrong chain alias reverts with a plain `require` string, not through `LibFhevmFail`. Fix: render the chain-table failures through `LibFhevmFail`.
- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/LibFhevmFail.sol:342-349` shows the NO PLAINTEXT SOURCE message, which names a replay and can no longer fire, because `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/FhevmVm.sol:1265` always sets the plaintext source. Fix: delete `noPlaintextsSource`.

Issues: I-34.

Everything that can go wrong because a
test is SET UP wrong — the `fhevm` handle missing, a fork entered through `vm` instead of `fhevm` (drift),
a fork whose stack was never named, a chain running a protocol version this SDK does not vendor, a
deployer nonce that is not where the local deploy expects it, a cheat called on the wrong kind of stack —
reverts with an ASCII-decorated, multi-line message that says WHAT happened, WHY it is refused, and the
exact line that FIXES it. Never a bare `EvmError: Revert`, never "call to non-contract address", never a
custom error whose selector the user has to decode. The measure: a developer who has never read this
package's source pastes the message and knows what to type next. Detect at the point closest to the
cause — `setUp`, a constructor, the first SDK entry — not where the consequence surfaces. All such
messages go through one helper so they look alike; tests match them with the same helper, so a reworded
message is a one-line change. (Errors that are NOT setup issues — a permit the ACL refuses, a handle the
replay never saw — stay typed custom errors: they are what a test asserts on.)

<a id="fr-16"></a>

## FR-16: Forking is automatic `[CONFLICT]`

> One `fhevm.createSelectFork` call prepares the fork, and the default stack is the local cleartext one.

Old number: 2.12.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- Conflicts with FR-33.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-39: Is `setProtocol` a user path, or internal?

Issues: I-13, I-39.

A test forks with
`fhevm.createSelectFork(getFhevmChain(group, alias), block)` and the SDK does the rest THE MOMENT THE
CALL RETURNS: version gate, signer sets swapped so proofs built here are accepted, the stack upgraded to
a cleartext one ([FR-19b](../entries/FR-19b.md)), protocol pointed. `fhevm.selectFork` re-points on every switch. By default — before any fork,
from `StdFhevm`'s constructor — the current stack is the local cleartext one; a URL-only fork CLEARS it
until the first SDK entry resolves the stack from the dApp that entry names or from the chain table. A
user never writes `setProtocol`, `defineCleartextContexts`, `addExecutor` or `registerFork`; `setUp` on a
fork needs nothing from us, and `super.setUp()` is not required. BORN ON A FORK (`forge test --fork-url`)
is the one fork nobody announces: `fhevm` takes its birth context as the drift baseline, `StdFhevm`'s
constructor deploys nothing on it (the chain is real; the deployer account may have history), and the
stack is resolved at the first entry like a URL-only fork's. `test/forkurl/` runs only in that mode
(`npm run test:fork-url`).

[FORK_AND_LOCAL.md](../../FORK_AND_LOCAL.md) explains how one API works on a local stack and on a fork.

<a id="fr-17"></a>

## FR-17: Two VMs, and which cheat goes through which `[STALE]`

> Fork cheats and `getRecordedLogs` go through `fhevm`, and every other cheat goes through `vm`.

Old number: 2.13.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- `LibFhevmFail.sol:65`, the FORK DRIFT message, says its FHE events were not drained, wording from the removed replay that this rule also uses. Fix: remove the drain wording from the rule and from the message.

Issues: I-12.

`fhevm` for the cheats this SDK has to stand in
front of — the fork family (`createSelectFork`, `createFork`, `selectFork`, `rollFork`, `activeFork`, `useStack`) and
`getRecordedLogs` — `vm` for everything else. A fork entered or switched through `vm` is FORK DRIFT and
is refused loudly at the next SDK entry, never repaired by guessing: forge cannot tell `fhevm` that
`vm.createSelectFork` ran, so its FHE events were not drained and its stack was never named. A new
override goes on `fhevm`, never as a free function with a made-up name; `FhevmVm.sol`'s table is the
list. `fhevm` is a contract etched at `keccak256("fhevm cheat code")`, persistent and cheat-enabled
(`allowCheatcodes`: an etched account is neither the test nor something it created), and a call to it is
a REAL frame — it consumes a pending `vm.prank` / `vm.expectRevert` ([FR-42](../entries/FR-42.md)).

<a id="fr-18"></a>

## FR-18: Anvil is a first-class target `[HOLD]`

> A fork of a running anvil gets the cleartext stack on first contact.

Old number: 2.14.

Check: missing.

Issues: I-14.

A fork of a running anvil gets the cleartext stack on first
contact: found at the canonical local addresses, or deployed into the fork (the local run's deploy,
verbatim) and mirrored onto the node with anvil's setters unless `fhevm.setAnvilMirror(false)`. Anvil is
the `local` group in the chain table, an SDK-only name outside the closed set of network groups. Two
facts the code carries: forge's `rpc` cheat encodes a bare JSON `true` as one word, not ABI `bytes`, so
anvil's setters are called raw and the mirror is verified by reading the node back; and a fresh anvil is
at block 0 while the executor derives handles from `blockhash(block.number - 1)`, so the SDK rolls the
fork to block 1 and mines one on the node.

[FORK_AND_LOCAL.md](../../FORK_AND_LOCAL.md) explains how one API works on a local stack and on a fork.

<a id="fr-19"></a>

## FR-19: A wrong protocol line fails by name `[VIOLATED]`

> On first contact with a fork, a host contract outside the vendored line fails by name, and any release of that line is accepted.

Old number: 2.15.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- The comments at `FhevmVm.sol:865-869` say the gate refuses an unsupported cleartext fork and checks all seven host contracts, and `FhevmVm.sol:152-153` says it does not. Fix: depends on D3.
- `FhevmVm.sol:986` says the floors are fhevm v0.13.0, and they are v0.14.0. Fix: correct the comment.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-30: Must the version gate refuse an unsupported cleartext fork, and check all seven host contracts?

Issues: I-12, I-30.

On first contact with a fork, every host contract's `getVersion()` must fall within the line
this SDK vendors: from what the line first shipped (`LibFhevmVersion.*_FLOOR`, hand-written from the
`v<N>.0` tag) up to what this SDK vendors (`LocalHostVersions`, generated), inclusive. Chains do not all
upgrade the same day — Sepolia ran `FHEVMExecutor v0.4.0` after this SDK vendored 0.13.6's `v0.5.0` — and
every release of a line speaks the ABI this SDK speaks, so an exact match would refuse stacks that work.
Outside the line it is the UNSUPPORTED PROTOCOL VERSION box, floor and ceiling against actual per
contract, never an attempt that dies in an ABI mismatch with an empty revert. New vendored release →
regenerate `LocalHostVersions` (`generate:contract-versions` in `<vN>`); new LINE → move the floors too, and
`LibFhevmVersion.t.sol` pins both.

<a id="fr-19a"></a>

## FR-19a: One generation back is upgraded on the fork `[STALE]`

> A stack one generation back is upgraded in memory on the fork instead of refused, in forge-fhevm-std only.

Old number: 2.15.1.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- `host-contracts-cleartext/v14/pkg/forge/src/LibForgeFhevmHostVersions.sol:108-121` shows the floors and ceilings of the previous line, which the rule places in `LibFhevmVersion`. Fix: name `LibForgeFhevmHostVersions`.
- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/FhevmVm.sol:935` shows `_upgradeCleartextIfOneGenerationBehind`, which also upgrades a cleartext stack one generation back, through `host-contracts-cleartext/v14/pkg/forge/src/LibForgeFhevmUpgrade.sol:292`. Fix: add the cleartext case.

Issues: I-21.

A stack whose versions are all on the PREVIOUS line — that line's own floors and ceilings,
hand-written in `LibFhevmVersion` and compared on major.minor only, since a generation is the shape of an
ABI and not a patch number — is brought forward in memory, on the fork, by
`LibForgeFhevmUpgrade.upgradeFromPreviousGeneration`: the same implementations and the same reinitializers
`pkg/ts/upgrade.ts` sends on a real chain, deployed patched for the fork's own addresses ([FR-26](../entries/FR-26.md)) and pranked
as `ACL.owner()`. Then rule [FR-19](../entries/FR-19.md)'s gate runs, unchanged, and an upgrade that half worked is refused by it
exactly as an unupgraded stack would be. This reaches exactly one generation: `<vN-2>` is refused, because
chaining two upgrades would rehearse a path nothing else rehearses. It does NOT loosen [FR-19](../entries/FR-19.md) in the other
direction — an older SDK on a newer chain stays refused, because it cannot know what the newer line does —
and no other SDK gets it: a Hardhat test is not on a copy of the chain, and the upgrade would be real.

<a id="fr-19b"></a>

## FR-19b: Every forked stack becomes a cleartext stack `[CONFLICT]`

> On first contact, the SDK points every forked stack at the cleartext implementations, and reads values from them.

Old number: 2.15.2.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- `CleartextForgeHCULimit.sol:63` declares its own storage, so the claim that the subclasses declare no state is false. Fix: correct the rule text.

Issues: I-12, I-13, I-21.

On first
contact `createSelectFork` re-points the fork's own proxies at this package's cleartext implementations
(`LibForgeFhevmUpgrade.upgradeToCleartext`), so the chain holds the plaintext of everything it computes
and `stack.plaintexts` is always the executor. It replaced an event processor that rebuilt those values
by replaying the executor's announcements — a second implementation of every operator, living in the
test process, which had to see every event or lose track of a value.

IN MEMORY, ON THE FORK. Nothing is broadcast. The real chain keeps answering its own version, which the
fork suites assert by taking a second plain fork afterwards.

THE LOGIC IS STILL THE CHAIN'S. Each cleartext contract EXTENDS the production one it replaces —
`CleartextFHEVMExecutor is FHEVMExecutor` — and every override runs `super` first, so handle derivation,
ACL checks and HCU accounting are the deployed code's. What is added is the bookkeeping beside it. That
is also why the swap is layout-safe with no reinitializer: the subclasses declare no state of their own.

THE FORGE VARIANTS WHERE THEY EXIST (ACL, executor, HCULimit, arithmetic), because a fork should behave
like a local stack: metering paused around the mock's own work, forge's randomness, the per-handle record
of [FR-19c](../entries/FR-19c.md). They call cheatcodes, and forge grants those per address to what IT created — a forked chain's
proxy is not that, so each is granted explicitly. Miss one and the stack reverts at its first FHE
operation.

A STACK THAT IS ALREADY CLEARTEXT keeps its own store, and the upgrade preserves it: only code changes.

[FORK_AND_LOCAL.md](../../FORK_AND_LOCAL.md) explains how one API works on a local stack and on a fork.

<a id="fr-19c"></a>

## FR-19c: A handle the stack did not compute is answered by policy `[CONFLICT]`

> A handle that the stack did not compute gets a stated value or a value from a per-type policy, or is refused, and is never invented silently.

Old number: 2.15.3.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- Conflicts with FR-25.
- FR-25 states this rule again for a handle minted before the fork: the test states its value or picks a per-type policy. Fix: merge FR-25 into this rule.
- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/StdFhevmCheats.sol:312` shows `forkUnknown(euint32 value, uint32 clear)`, and the rule writes `forkUnknown(handle, value)`. Fix: write `forkUnknown(value, clear)`.

Issues: I-13, I-21.

On a fork most store misses are handles minted before the cleartext layer existed, and a test
says what they are: `forkUnknown(handle, value)` states one, or a per-type default or `keccak(handle)`
derivation answers for all of that type (`CleartextForgeArithmetic`). Per TYPE, not globally: one number
cannot mean an address and a `euint8` at once, and the width would silently truncate it.

A MISS IS NOT ALWAYS AN OLD HANDLE, and the difference must not be guessed. The HCU limit meters every
handle the executor computes, so a reading there means THIS stack produced it — and a handle it produced
that the cleartext layer did not record is an operator the mirror does not override, which no policy may
cover. Checked before any policy, and refused by its own name.

<a id="fr-20"></a>

## FR-20: forge-std stops at `pkg/src/` `[VIOLATED]`

> Files in `pkg/src/_host/` import nothing from forge-std, and files in `pkg/src/` use forge-std wherever it has the type.

Old number: 2.16.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/StdFhevm.sol:75`, `StdFhevmDecrypt.sol:74,83,101,110` and `StdFhevmCheats.sol:209` call `fvm`, the vendored `IForgeVm` that `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/_host/ForgeVmBase.sol:13` declares, where forge-std's `Vm` has the same functions. Fix: use forge-std's `Vm` in `pkg/src/*.sol`.
- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/_host/LibForgeFhevmHCU.sol:157` and `LibForgeFhevmHostVersions.sol:67` mention forge-std in comments, so `grep -rl forge-std pkg/src/_host` lists four files, not the two that the rule names. Fix: make the check search for imports only, and name no files.

#### Where the code lives

Everything under `pkg/src/_host/` is generated. It is a copy of `host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg/forge/src/`, and the generator deletes the destination before it copies (`rmSync(pkg/src/_host)`). An edit made there is lost on the next `npm run generate`, with no conflict and no warning.

```
host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg/src/cleartext/shared/   <- source of the shared libraries
        |  generate:forge-shared   (rm -rf destination, then copy)
        v
host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg/forge/src/shared/       <- generated
host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg/forge/src/*.sol         <- source of the forge payload
        |  generate:forge-payload  (rm -rf destination, then copy)
        v
foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/_host/                    <- generated
```

#### Where forge-std stops

Two layers, two rules,
and the boundary is the directory:

- `pkg/src/_host/**` — the payload and its shared libraries — imports NOTHING from `forge-std`. The forge
  VM is reached through the vendored `IForgeVm` / `FORGE_VM_ADDRESS` (`_host/IForgeVm.sol`) and nothing
  else. The payload is copied into other packages and consumed by projects whose `lib/forge-std` wins the
  remapping; a `forge-std` import there would pin every consumer to one forge-std version for a file that
  is declarations only.
- `pkg/src/*.sol` — `StdFhevm*`, `TestFhevm`, `FhevmVm`, the `Lib*` this package owns — MAY and, where
  forge-std has the type, MUST use `forge-std`: `Vm`, `VmSafe`, `Test`, `Vm.Log`. This package IS a
  forge-std extension; `TestFhevm is Test, StdFhevm` is its whole reason to exist, and a test that
  inherits it already depends on `forge-std`. Hiding that behind the vendored interface would give the
  same code two spellings of one VM and two `Log` types to convert between at every boundary.

The original goal was "no forge-std dependency anywhere". It is not reachable: `TestFhevm` must inherit
forge-std's `Test`, so the dependency exists the moment a test is written. The rule is therefore about
WHERE it lives, not whether. Mechanical check: `grep -rl forge-std pkg/src/_host` must list only comment
mentions (`IForgeVm.sol`, `ForgeVmBase.sol` explain their own vendoring), never an `import`.

## FR-24: A fork needs signers, and the SDK swaps them `[STALE]`

> On first contact with a fork, and after each roll, the SDK swaps in signer sets that the test can sign as.

Old number: 3.2.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/FhevmVm.sol:857` calls `LibForgeFhevmStack.defineCleartextContexts`. `LibForgeFhevmContexts`, which the rule names, does not exist. Fix: name `LibForgeFhevmStack`.
- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/FhevmVm.sol:829-833` shows that a roll resets only `_forkPrepared`. No fork replay exists. Fix: remove the replay from the roll sentence.
- `host-contracts-cleartext/v14/pkg/forge/src/LibForgeFhevmStack.sol:532-552` shows that the KMS signer swap needs committee confirmations and an epoch activation after the owner's proposal, so both levers are not only `onlyACLOwner`. Fix: describe the v14 steps.

A production `InputVerifier` is
registered against coprocessor signers nobody here holds a key for. On first contact with a fork,
`fhevm` swaps both sets — `LibForgeFhevmContexts.defineCleartextContexts`, pranking `ACL.owner()`, no
storage patching, both levers `onlyACLOwner` — once per fork, and again after `fhevm.rollFork` — a roll resets the fork's local state, the swap and the
fork's replay with it, so a rolled fork is prepared like a fresh fork at that block (pre-roll handles are
unknown to it; `forkUnknown` states them again). A cleartext stack (anvil) is skipped: it registers the
cleartext signers itself.

## FR-26: Two different address techniques `[STALE]`

> Templates keep placeholder markers that the deploy patches, and `LocalHostBytecode.sol` is rebuilt with the real addresses.

Old number: 4.1.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/_host/LibForgeFhevmUpgrade.sol:197,265,309` show that `LibHostUpgradeCode.creationCodeFor` also patches for the cleartext swap (`upgradeToCleartext`) and for the cleartext generation upgrade, and the rule permits it for the one-generation upgrade only. Fix: list the three uses. The fix depends on D11.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-36: Does a rule that repeats one sentence of another rule count as `[CONFLICT]`?
- Pending owner decision, issue I-38: Is the bytecode patching meant for all three upgrade paths, or only the one-generation upgrade?

Issues: I-36, I-38, I-122.

- **Templates** (`generate:templates`) keep placeholder markers — addresses derived as
  `keccak256("fhevm.placeholder.<NAME>")[0:20]` — compiled in as literals, and record the byte
  offsets where they land so the TS deploy can overwrite them at deploy time. Hence the ordering: the
  placeholder file is written _before_ `forge build`, or the previous run's markers stay baked in at
  the recorded offsets.
- **`LocalHostBytecode.sol`** (`generate:local-host-bytecode`) deliberately does NOT patch for the
  local deploy. It derives the deployer from the mnemonic, precomputes the nonce sequence's addresses,
  writes them as a real config, rebuilds, and reads the creation bytecode straight out of the artifacts.
  ONE EXCEPTION, and only this one: the upgrade tables it also emits (`*_UPGRADE_CREATION_CODE`,
  `*_UPGRADE_SITES`) exist so [FR-19a](../entries/FR-19a.md) can deploy those same host implementations beside a REMOTE stack,
  whose addresses are not known at generation time and cannot be compiled in. That patching is
  `LibHostUpgradeCode`, it is cheatcode-free and pure, and it is permitted for upgrading an existing
  deployed remote non-cleartext stack one generation behind — for nothing else. In particular the local
  deploy still recompiles, and the generator measures every site's offset in the blob it SHIPS rather
  than reusing the template offsets: solc pools address constants by value, so two builds order them
  differently (`POOL_REORDER_EXEMPT` is that same fact, from the other side).

Old number: 4.2.

Check: missing.

Issues: I-14, I-122.

It records how many bytecode sites each

<a id="fr-28"></a>

## FR-28: After touching a cleartext contract `[HOLD]`

> After you change a cleartext contract, regenerate and test the host package, then regenerate this package.

Old number: 4.3.

Check: missing.

Issues: I-01, I-14, I-15, I-36.

A cleartext contract has its source in the host package, `host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>`. This package
holds only a generated copy of it, in `pkg/src/_host/` ([FR-20](../entries/FR-20.md)). A change reaches this package
only when both packages generate again, in this order:

1. In the host package, run `npm run generate`. It rebuilds the files generated from the contracts,
   including the bytecode that the test stack deploys.
2. In the host package, run `forge test`. It tests the change in the package where you made it.
3. In this package, run `npm run generate`. It copies the new payload of the host package into
   `pkg/src/_host/`.

For example, you fix a bug in `CleartextFHEVMExecutor.sol`:

```bash
cd host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>
# You edit pkg/src/cleartext/CleartextFHEVMExecutor.sol.
npm run generate   # 1. Rebuilds the generated files and the bytecode.
forge test         # 2. Tests the fix in the host package.
cd ../../foundry/forge-fhevm-std
npm run generate   # 3. Copies the fix into pkg/src/_host/.
```

If you skip step 3, the tests of this package still run the old copy, without your fix, and pass.

If the contract is `CleartextFHEVMExecutor`, also check
`ContractSizeLimits.t.sol` — it must stay under EIP-170, while the `…Forge` variant is exempt and
deliberately over. `FhevmVm` is exempt too: it is ETCHED (`vm.etch` skips the creation-time check) and may
grow past 24 KB by design; write no size test against it.

#### Before you push

Run these checks, first in the host package, which is the source, then in this package, which consumes it:

```bash
# The host package, the source.
cd host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>
npm run generate && npm run forge:fmt && npm run forge:lint && forge test
MAINNET_RPC_URL=… forge test --match-contract Fork

# This package, the consumer. From the workspace root, the same runs through make:
#   make compile-forge-std lint-forge-std test-forge-std     # or everything: make ci-fast
cd ../../foundry/forge-fhevm-std
npm run generate && npm run lint && forge test
npm run test:consumer                    # the installed @fhevm/forge, by name (FR-04)
SEPOLIA_RPC_URL=… MAINNET_RPC_URL=… npm run test:fork
ARBITRUM_RPC_URL=… MAINNET_RPC_URL=… npm run test:fork        # adds the cleartext-on-a-foreign-chain suite (FR-21)
ARBITRUM_RPC_URL=… MAINNET_RPC_URL=… npm run test:fork-debug  # the same under the fhevm-debug profile (FR-22)
SEPOLIA_RPC_URL=… npm run test:fork-url  # the born-on-a-fork suite, under `forge test --fork-url`
npm run test:anvil                       # starts a throwaway anvil on 8546, runs test/anvil, stops it
```

Use the npm scripts of the host package, not bare `forge fmt` or `forge lint`. The host package keeps the payload under a second profile (`src = pkg/forge/src`), so a bare command formats and lints only `pkg/src`, and reports a clean payload it never looked at. `forge:fmt` and `forge:lint` run all three profiles. The gap does not show in the host package. It shows here, on the generated copy.

If a test says "No tests found in project!" right after you restore or rename a file, the cause is the incremental cache of forge, not the test. Run `forge build --force`, then run the test again.

Both packages end with zero lint notes, zero unused imports, and a clean `forge fmt --check`.

For a stack-too-deep check, loop on `forge build --skip test`, which takes about 0.7 seconds. `forge test` alone does not see a source change that must pass through `generate` to reach the deployed bytecode. The stack is deployed from bytecode generated beforehand, so an edit that is not regenerated tests nothing.

<a id="fr-29"></a>

## FR-29: `Forge` in a name means it touches cheatcodes `[CONFLICT]`

> A name contains `Forge` only when its code uses cheatcodes.

Old number: 5.1.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- Conflicts with FR-05.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-29: Does "carries `Forge` in its name" apply to every file in `pkg/src` that uses the VM, or only to host source and `_host/`?

Issues: I-13, I-29.

A reader must be able to tell from the file
list alone which code can never run on chain.

#### Name a file

For names, follow forge-std first. Where forge-std says nothing, follow this table:

| Kind                          | Pattern                                                             | Example                                             |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| library                       | `Lib<Name>.sol`                                                     | `LibKmsVerifier`, `LibFheType`                      |
| library that uses cheatcodes  | `LibForgeFhevm<Name>.sol`                                           | `LibForgeFhevmEncrypt`, `LibForgeFhevmHostVersions` |
| contract that uses cheatcodes | `ForgeFhevm<Name>.sol`                                              | `ForgeFhevmDeploy`                                  |
| public API mixin              | `StdFhevm<Name>.sol`                                                | `StdFhevmEncrypt`, `StdFhevmDecrypt`                |
| cheats mixin                  | `…CheatsSafe`, with `…Cheats is …CheatsSafe` once a footgun appears | forge-std's `StdCheatsSafe`                         |
| interface                     | `I<Name>.sol`                                                       | `IForgeVm`, `IPlaintexts`                           |
| argument bundle               | `<Function>ArgsV1`                                                  | `UserDecryptPayloadArgsV1`                          |
| pinned to an ABI shape        | `V1`, last                                                          | `userDecryptV1OnForkStack`                          |

`Forge` in a name means cheatcodes, and nothing else. `LibHostUpgradeCode` patches bytecode and is pure, so its name has no `Forge`. `Host` in place of `Fhevm` means the host contracts rather than the SDK. That is why the version tables are `LibForgeFhevmHostVersions`: they use cheatcodes, and they are about the hosts.

entry in `foundry.toml` or a `SEPOLIA_RPC_URL` variable, never for the built-in default — plus `vm.skip`, so
the offline suite stays green and either forge-native way to name a URL opts a suite in. Assert `block.chainid` in `setUp` when the addresses are chain-specific.

<a id="fr-39"></a>

## FR-39: Assert events with `vm.expectEmit` `[HOLD]`

> Assert events with `vm.expectEmit`, and record logs only where a test needs the array.

Old number: 7.4.

Check: missing.

Issues: I-14, I-35.

`expectEmit` consumes nothing and reads better than
scanning an array. `vm.recordLogs()` / `vm.getRecordedLogs()` are fine where a test genuinely wants the
array — they are forge's, used as forge documents them. There was once an SDK wrapper to prefer instead,
because the buffer had a second reader; there is not, because it does not ([FR-07](../entries/FR-07.md)).

<a id="fr-40"></a>

## FR-40: No `vm.setEnv` in a test that asserts on it `[HOLD]`

> A test never sets with `vm.setEnv` a value that it asserts on, because forge runs test contracts in parallel.

Old number: 7.5.

Check: missing.

Issues: I-14.

It mutates the process environment and forge
runs test contracts in parallel, so such a test races every other suite. Test the rule through a
parameter instead.

<a id="fr-41"></a>

## FR-41: `setUp` runs once per contract `[HOLD]`

> Forge runs `setUp` once per test contract and restores its state before each test.

Old number: 7.6.

Check: impossible.

Forge snapshots the state it produced and restores that
before each test. Cheatcode state armed there (a log recorder) is restored with it; a side effect
outside the snapshot — a file write, an env write — happens once, not once per test.

<a id="fr-42"></a>

## FR-42: Hoist calls out of argument position `[HOLD]`

> Move an external call out of the arguments of a call that a pending `vm.prank` or `vm.expectRevert` targets.

Old number: 7.7.

Check: missing.

Issues: I-14.

An external call in an argument consumes a pending
`vm.prank` or `vm.expectRevert` before the intended call sees it. (A _cheatcode_ call does not —
that one is safe.)
